explanation: In marine ecosystems, the euphotic zone represents the shallow surface waters that receive sunlight. It contains a higher concentration of marine organisms than the deeper parts of the ocean. Coral reefs are located just below the surface in shallow, warm, tropical waters, and are densely populated with life.

questions.q: Which ocean zone contains the highest concentration of marine organisms due to sunlight availability?
questions.exp: The notes state that the 'Euphotic Zone (shallow ocean waters)' contains a 'greater concentration of organisms than the rest of the sea.'

opts: In the deep abyssal plain near hydrothermal vents
Just below the surface in shallow, warm, tropical waters
